# Breath and trees: two routes, and clusters. Findings 002

*Generated by `uv run python -m knots_sim.export` on 2026-09-26 (inputs 2b25b0ebc678). Every number comes from that
run. The model is `sim/knots_sim/models/vessel.py` (the movement route) and `sim/knots_sim/models/tree.py`; the trials
are `sim/knots_sim/breath.py`. The site shows the same results at /research/.*

## In brief

1. **The breath has two routes, and the model now carries both.** Through drive, as before. Through movement: a change of
   shape loosens the wall's force for a while, saturating, fitted to squeezed arteries (clifford2006): +14%
   after one 1 s squeeze (measured +16%), +15% after one of 5 s
   (+14%), +25% after five (+27%), peaking
   2.1–4.3 s after release (measured 2.8–4.6 s).
   The wall answers changes of shape, not held shapes, so the loosening adds up over breaths.
2. **An even breath holds every knot; easy knots go first; the deepest hold.** Over 30 slow breaths:

   (Columns: how far above its own reopening threshold the drive holding the knot sits, as a share of the band.)
3. **What would have to be true for movement to be the route**: the least deformation per breath, as a share of a squeeze
   that shuts the vessel:

| within | 1% | 5% | 10% | 20% | 35% | 50% | 65% | 80% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 breaths | 10% | 12% | 15% | 21% | 31% | 40% | 48% | 57% |
| 10 breaths | 1% | 4% | 7% | 13% | 23% | 32% | 42% | 52% |

4. **One breath or many turns on how fast the skin's small arteries ease when drive falls.** With the value fitted to the
   gasp's recovery (12 s), an uneven breath (−0.06) releases the easiest knot after
   42 s; if they eased in 3 s, after 11 s. Nobody has measured it over hairy skin.
5. **Broad or focused.** On a patch of 240 perforators, each with its own wall and more stress in some zones,
   63 knots form under strong regional stress. With no breath, 5 poised at their
   thresholds drift open. When drive eases everywhere (broad), 35 let go, scattered across the patch,
   in order of difficulty (correlation of depth and release time 0.98). When the breath moves the tissue around one spot (focused), 9
   of the 12 knots within a radius of the spot let go and 9 of the
   51 elsewhere. Together, 12 of 12 at the spot and
   33 of 51 elsewhere. (The zones, the patch and the spot are representative.)
6. **One knot upstream makes a cluster below it.** In the worked tree (a parent and four children with walls from 0.25 to
   0.35, as in hypertension, drive 0.40), a local surge shuts the parent at 12 s and all four children within 3.4 s,
   as the pressure below the parent collapses. Released after a 40 s press, the parent reopens at 140 s and
   3 children with it within 5 s; the last lets go at 232 s, after drive falls to rest.
7. **Across 256 plausible trees** (pressures, the parent's resistance, the children's walls and the drive
   sampled): when the parent held a knot, a cluster formed beneath it in 97% (3.1
   of 4 children on average); releasing the parent freed most of its cluster within 5 s in 91%; at
   least one child stayed held in 33%. In the worked tree, the higher the drive, the longer the queue
   (drive: children left held) 0.34: 0, 0.38: 1, 0.42: 1, 0.46: 2, 0.50: 2, 0.54: 2, 0.58: 3.
8. **Siblings on one feed protect each other.** Each closure raises the pressure holding the others open: a surge of
   stress shut 4 of 8, where alone, at the same pressure, 8 would. Clusters come
   from the tree's hierarchy.

## Limits

- The movement route is calibrated on rat muscle feed arteries squeezed shut, not on skin; how much a breath deforms the
  tissue at a knot is unmeasured, so it is swept.
- The tree's resistances and pressures are guesses, sampled across ranges; a real tree branches further.
- The author's observation that a parent's release frees its children (O13) was written down after these runs were
  shared: the match is found after the fact.
- These are what the mechanisms can do with measured numbers. They measure nothing.
